subject.title: Memory MVP: add review, edit, forget, and conflict-resolution flows

question: Should the durable memory lifecycle MVP live in the default memory-core plugin, in memory-wiki's knowledge workflows, or behind a new/expanded memory plugin API first?
rationale: The request defines storage semantics, audit/privacy behavior, and operator UX across active memory and wiki/plugin boundaries, so maintainer intent is needed before implementation.

options.title: Design memory-core lifecycle MVP first
options.body: Make memory-core own the v1 typed lifecycle schema and expose narrow review, edit, tombstone/forget, supersede, and conflict-resolution flows.

options.title: Route through memory-wiki
options.body: Treat the work as provenance-rich knowledge curation and extend memory-wiki claim, lint, and apply flows before changing active memory records.

options.title: Define plugin API seams first
options.body: Add a memory lifecycle SDK contract so bundled and external memory plugins can implement the flows consistently before choosing the default implementation.

recommendation.title: Design memory-core lifecycle MVP first
recommendation.body: Make memory-core own the v1 typed lifecycle schema and expose narrow review, edit, tombstone/forget, supersede, and conflict-resolution flows.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent memory-wiki and memory-area history makes this the best available owner for product/API direction among the likely routing candidates.
